title: Migrate Python identity.py derivation to upstream AddrForKey/SubnetForKey
description: Python half of the i72x upstream-Yggdrasil migration (mirrors i72x.1 C, i72x.2 Rust commit 5c9f7ef657). python/src/lichen/crypto/identity.py yggdrasil_address() (lines ~206-234) still implements the REJECTED SHA-512 native profile (addr=[0x02]+SHA-512(pubkey)[0:7]+IID). Replace with upstream AddrForKey byte-for-byte (bit-invert 32-byte pubkey; addr[0]=0x02; addr[1]=leading-1 count mod 256; skip leading 1s + first 0 separator bit; pack remaining bits MSB-first into whole bytes, discard trailing partial; addr[2:16] zero tail; no hashing — yggdrasil-go@422836ee src/address/address.go). Add subnet_for_key() = AddrForKey[0:8] with byte0|=0x01 (0300::/8). KEEP _pubkey_to_iid (SHA-512 IID) UNCHANGED — link-local only. Sweep Python callers relying on the dead IID-embedding invariant (addr bytes 8:16 == SHA-512 IID). Oracle discipline: pin expected bytes from upstream address_test.go (anchor pubkey bdbacfd8..6efb -> 0200848a604fbb7e438465db8db66895, subnet 0300848a604fbb7e); cross-check against the independent Rust impl (i72x.2), NEVER self-derived. Update Python tests that consume the rejected native profile; leave shared corpora to i72x.6. This unblocks i72x.6 (corpus regen). Verify: pytest python/ green.
close_reason: Migrated python/src/lichen/crypto/identity.py to upstream Yggdrasil addressing (committed via worker4 sync 9fceaf5406, now on main). yggdrasil_address() now implements upstream AddrForKey byte-for-byte (bit-invert 32-byte pubkey; addr[0]=0x02; addr[1]=leading-1 count mod 256 w/ Go byte-overflow semantics; skip leading 1s + first 0 separator; pack remaining bits MSB-first into whole bytes, discard trailing partial; addr[2:16] zero tail; no hashing — yggdrasil-go@422836ee src/address/address.go). Added subnet_for_key() (AddrForKey[0:8], byte0|=0x01 -> 0300::/8). _pubkey_to_iid (SHA-512 IID, link-local) UNCHANGED. ORACLE DISCIPLINE: never self-derived — pinned from upstream address_test.go anchor (bdbacfd8..6efb -> 0200848a604fbb7e438465db8db66895 / subnet 0300848a604fbb7e) AND cross-validated byte-exact against the independent Rust impl (i72x.2) across 7 degenerate/boundary key shapes (all-zero, all-ff, first/last/mid-bit-set, alternating, leading-ones-run) — ALL MATCH. TESTS MIGRATED (green): test_yggdrasil_address_vectors.py (anchor -> byte-equality + subnet + degenerate + no-IID-embedding), test_identity.py (hardcoded native -> upstream values), test_addr.py + test_key_address_cross_impl_vectors.py (dropped stale-corpus native pins per their own 'delete on migration' docstrings; replaced native oracle with an independent upstream AddrForKey oracle). Derivation suites: 90 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (test_committed_ipv6_address_vectors_match_stdlib_generator — 'atomic JSON parent directory is unsafe' generator env issue, fails on un-migrated code too). Codereview 3x: correctness PASS + security PASS via kimi-k3 reviewer; edge-cases self-verified via cross-impl oracle after reviewer timeout (fallback per protocol). DOWNSTREAM (NOT in scope, correctly red): corpus-bound tests reading stale shared corpora (root_dio_signature.json, dao_origin_signature.json, root_signature.json, tunnel_authorization.json, authenticated_schc_dio.json, yggdrasil-derivation.json, ipv6-addresses.json) are i72x.6's regeneration scope — left failing as the honest stale-oracle signal per project policy (report conflicting fixtures, don't weaken tests). dao_prefix_authorization failures are the dao_origin pin-by-IID production design gap -> filed o5bl. Full failing-test inventory commented on i72x.6.
